span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Species differ in place-cell abundance because the ecological demand for spatial memory differs: caching and homing species that must remember many locations develop robust place coding, species that do not need it show little
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because caching birds must retrieve many hidden items, selection for that behaviour is what produces the enlarged hippocampus and abundant place cells, so place cells are proposed to serve spatial memory rather than merely accompany it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Head direction tuning in a migratory seabird is anchored by the earth's magnetic field, the cells encoding head angle relative to magnetic north
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Knowing one's own place and heading requires converting head- and body-centred sensory input into an environment-fixed frame, a transformation performed in and upstream of the hippocampus
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The neural mechanisms of avian spatial cognition remain poorly understood.
span.note: what this limits: any mechanistic claim in the review: OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE NEURAL MECHANISMS OF SPATIAL COGNITION IN BIRDS IS STILL POOR
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: All avian hippocampal recordings so far come from small enclosures, unlike the scales at which birds actually navigate.
span.note: what this limits: every avian hippocampal recording in the literature: TO DATE, ALL THE EXPERIMENTS IN WHICH BRAIN ACTIVITY WAS RECORDED IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS OF BIRDS HAVE BEEN CONDUCTED IN RELATIVELY SMALL ENVIRONMENTS - unlike the scales at which birds navigate
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: How the earth's magnetic field shapes the avian head-direction system is not yet resolved.
span.note: what this limits: the magnetic-field question specifically: FURTHER EXAMINATION OF HEAD DIRECTION CELLS IN STREAKED SHEARWATER AND OTHER BIRDS IS NECESSARY TO RESOLVE HOW THE HEAD DIRECTION SYSTEM IN THE AVIAN HIPPOCAMPUS IS INFLUENCED BY THE EARTH'S MAGNETIC FIELD
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The category's criterion comes from another species, and 2% of the units tested meet it.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about place cells in birds: of more than 2,000 single units recorded in quail hippocampus, only about 2% passed the criterion for place cells, and most of those did not show the clear single field expected from the classical place cells found in rodents
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The structure is called a homologue and stated to differ fundamentally in architecture.
span.note: what this limits: any transfer of a mammalian hippocampal result to birds: the avian homologue of the mammalian hippocampus has an architecture that, after three hundred million years of independent evolution, differs fundamentally from the mammalian one

span.label: the avian hippocampus - A HOMOLOGUE THAT DIFFERS FUNDAMENTALLY: identified as the avian homologue of the mammalian hippocampus by development, connectivity and cellular markers, and stated in the next sentence to have an architecture fundamentally different after three hundred million years of independent evolution - the correspondence and the difference are asserted together

span.label: a cognitive map - A DIFFERENT ORDER OF MAGNITUDE IN BIRDS: the well-studied rodent maps cover small areas while avian maps must represent ranges of hundreds and thousands of kilometres, so the same term names representations whose spatial scale differs by several orders
